title: Good decision: Invalid Last-Event-ID silently ignored, no 400 error
description:
Decision: A Last-Event-ID header that doesn't match the expected format (s-\d+) or exceeds 64 bytes is silently treated as absent. The stream opens with 200 and proceeds normally, no 400 error.

Code location: lines 89-105 of kithd/src/events.rs. Tests: events_last_event_id_invalid_format_ignored and events_last_event_id_too_long_ignored.

Why this is correct: RFC 8895 (Server-Sent Events spec) says the client MAY send Last-Event-ID but doesn't mandate format. A malformed header from a buggy or non-compliant client shouldn't break the entire stream. Silent fallback (treat as absent) is more robust: the client loses the replay optimization but the stream works. If the format ever drifts, you learn via absence of expected replay events, not a hard 400 error that breaks compatibility.

Over-strict validation (400 on malformed LEI) is fragile in a distributed system where clients vary widely and sometimes send non-standard headers. Lenient parsing (skip and continue) is more forgiving.

The wrong alternative would be to return 400 Bad Request for any malformed Last-Event-ID. This breaks clients with slightly-nonstandard headers or would require tight coordination on exact format across many clients.
